verses.text: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered:
"Should all those words go unanswered? Does a flood of talk prove someone right?
Should your boasting silence everyone? Will no one put you to shame when you mock us?
You say, 'What I teach is pure, and I'm clean in your sight.'
If only God would speak and open his mouth to answer you.
If only he'd show you the secrets of wisdom, because true wisdom has more than one side. Then you'd know God is holding you to account for less than your guilt deserves.
Can you get to the bottom of God's mysteries? Can you find the limits of the Almighty?
They're as high as heaven. What can you do? They're deeper than Sheol. What can you know?
They stretch farther than the earth and wider than the sea.
If God passes by, locks someone up, or calls the court into session, who can stand in his way?
He knows who is false. He sees wrongdoing even without having to look for it.
A fool will become wise when a wild donkey gives birth to a human.
If you set your heart right, stretch out your hands to God.
If there's wrongdoing in your hands, put it far from you. Clear injustice out of your tents.
Then you'll be able to lift your face without shame. You'll stand firm and won't be afraid.
You'll forget your misery. You'll remember it only as water that has flowed past.
Your life will be brighter than noon. Even its darkness will be like morning.
You'll feel secure because there's hope. You'll look around and lie down safely.
You'll rest with no one to frighten you, and many people will seek your favor.
But the eyes of the wicked will fail. They won't find a way to escape. Their only hope will be to breathe their last."
